Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service New York NY
300 AM EST Fri Nov 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
The potential for flooding late Sunday into Monday has been 
included in the HWO.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
1) A coastal low will impact the area with wind and rain Sunday
into Monday. Minor coastal impacts possible due to approaching 
full moon on Tuesday.

2) Rain possible around Thanksgiving with another coastal storm,
but uncertainty is very high at this time.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
.KEY MESSAGE 1...
The 00Z models have converged on a general soln for the low Sun
and Mon, lending to increased confidence in a rainstorm across 
the area. The area is in a Marginal Risk for Excessive rainfall.
Refer to the NHC for any tropical/subtropical details.

The 00Z GFS, AI-GFS, RRFS, and ECMWF, among others, suggest a 
990s or so low passing thru or just east of the area Sun night 
into Mon. PWATS with the sys around 2 inches, but the low is 
modeled to track northward at about 20kt limiting the duration 
of the heavy rainfall. The trend indicates less interaction with
the upstream cold front, allowing for the more wly track, as 
well as a slight lowering of the overall rain potential. This is
only one model cycle of consensus however, so would expect some
additional challenges with the overall track and intensity of 
this storm given the complicated nature of the setup.

The trend for wind is down as well due to the weaker low and
potential track over the cwa. The coastal track however would
introduce an onshore component enhancing the coastal flood
threat. This may be offset by the weaker flow however. NYHOPS
guidance maintains primarily a non event most areas with some
minor flooding across the most vulnerable back bay spots. It
wouldn't be unreasonable to see the entire threat ramp up a
little should the track and intensity optimize, as evidenced by
Freeport touching moderate on the extreme high end of the
ensemble envelop, but this is not what the majority of the
current guidance suggests.


.KEY MESSAGE 2...
Extreme model disagreement for another potential coastal low for
around Thanksgiving. The ECMWF tracks the low over Cape Cod, the
AI-GFS east of Nantucket, and the GFS well south of the area as
a 1040 high over northern New England holds firm. The GEFS does
support a soln a bit further N as well, so it is possible the 
operational GFS is an outlier, although its consistency weakens
this theory.

Consensus pops via the NBM are around 60 percent for the event,
with the pcpn primarily rain. Some mixing could be possible
across the interior particularly at the onset, but overall this
looks to be another wind and rain event if it materializes.

&&

.AVIATION /07Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
High pressure remains in control through the TAF period. 

VFR. Some outlying terminals, like KISP, may have some shallow
fog with localized conditions dropping to as low as IFR through
the early morning.

W/SW flow under 10 kt through Friday afternoon, becoming more N/NW 
Friday night at 5 kt or less. Some typical outlying terminals may be 
VRB tonight and Friday night.

 ...NY Metro (KEWR/KLGA/KJFK/KTEB) TAF Uncertainty...

No unscheduled amendments expected.

.OUTLOOK FOR 06Z Saturday through Tuesday... 

Friday Night-Saturday: VFR.

Sunday: Chance of MVFR or lower conditions developing in RA.

Monday: MVFR or lower likely early in RA, improvement possible PM. 
NW G20-25kt.

Tuesday: VFR. Weakening NW flow.

Detailed information, including hourly TAF wind component forecasts, 
can be found at: https:/www.weather.gov/zny/n90

&&

.MARINE...
Winds and seas will remain below SCA lvls thru Sat. Low pres 
will produce building seas and increasing winds Sun into Mon. 
Seas on the ocean could build to 5 ft or greater by the end of 
the day Sun, with small craft or gale force winds possible on 
all waters Mon depending on the track and intensity of the low.
NW winds behind the storm will likely reach SCA lvls on Tue, 
especially on the ocean.
